clue.text: Direction to slow down tune trio ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of these two words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A conductor's instruction to slow a melody that three players have already made a mess of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges TUNETRIO into the Italian musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritenuto is an Italian musical marking telling performers to hold back the tempo at once.

clue.text: New name given Jane, after moving east

indicators.note: after moving signals that one letter of the given name shifts to a new position

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Jane is renamed after relocating to the eastern side of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after moving' shifts the E of JANE forward so it follows the J. One of the puzzle's themed name changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is a girl's forename, here the fresh name that a rearranged Jane takes on.

clue.text: One rule I had set up for Indian festival

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the whole string is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a law is a rule
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone describes arranging a rule of their own for a celebration in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns I + LAW + ID as a block, giving DI + WAL + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights celebrated across India each autumn.

clue.text: Fearful hen I can, oddly, put in kind of curry

parts.note: chicken is slang for cowardly, fearful

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A timid hen ends up being cooked into a curry dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges HENICAN. The curry is chicken Madras, with Madras given its new name, Chennai, in line with the puzzle's theme of name changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken Madras is a familiar curry-house dish; Madras is now officially Chennai, so the renamed dish follows.

clue.text: Stone block with solid middle installed in part of year

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside another word

parts.note: a month is a part of a year

indicators.note: middle picks the central letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A heavy block of stone with a solid core is put in place at some point in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle' picks the central three letters of 'solid', and 'installed in' sets them inside the calendar unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A monolith is a single large upright block of stone, like a standing stone.

clue.text: Dainty little daughter covering one leg, as requested

indicators.note: covering means the first pieces wrap around the second ones

parts.note: petite means dainty and small
one is the Roman numeral I
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A dainty little girl hides a leg under her dress, as she was asked to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts ION inside PETITED, between PETIT and ED. ON for leg is a cricket convention: the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition is to make a formal request, so petitioned is a past-tense synonym for asked.

clue.text: What Blair became before spring

parts.note: or is an old poetic word for before, as in 'or ever'
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A question about what the politician Blair turned into before the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blair is not Tony but Eric Blair, who took the pen name George Orwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Arthur Blair wrote under the pseudonym George Orwell, so that is the name he became known by.

clue.text: Players collectively demolish extra food

parts.note: a side is a team of players
to dish is to ruin or demolish, as in dishing someone's hopes

explanation.surface: A team of players wolfs down an additional plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A side dish is extra food served alongside the main course.

clue.text: Old king's literary pseudonym

parts.note: Henry is the name of many English kings

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch writes under an assumed name.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is just a link (king is), not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: O. Henry was the pen name of the American short-story writer William Sydney Porter.

clue.text: Name of man backing another in Spanish city

indicators.note: backing means read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Noel is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man's name sits behind another man's name in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NOEL around, which also gives another man's name, hence 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: León is a historic city in north-western Spain.

clue.text: Solitary types disoriented in chain store

indicators.note: disoriented means confused and out of place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Loners get lost inside a big chain store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disoriented' rearranges CHAINSTORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorites are religious hermits who live in seclusion, so they are solitary people.

clue.text: Mother has to purchase, we hear, dear kind of fish

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
duck is a British term of endearment, like dear

explanation.surface: Mum has to buy an expensive type of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: BAI sounds like 'buy'. The fish is Bombay duck, with Bombay renamed Mumbai as in the theme. 'Duck' meaning dear is everyday northern English.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay duck is a lizardfish eaten dried in India; Bombay is now Mumbai, so the name follows.

clue.text: Asian citizen I see being mistreated around judge

indicators.note: around means the anagrammed letters go round another letter
mistreated means badly handled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sees a citizen being ill-treated near a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' rearranges ISEEBEING, and 'around' wraps it about J. The word plays on Pekingese, with Peking renamed Beijing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Beijingese is a native or inhabitant of Beijing, the capital of China in Asia.

clue.text: Fit for match between the Spanish and the French, one great back

indicators.note: between means placed in the middle of two other pieces

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
le is French for the
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: back means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: big means great

explanation.surface: A great player returns between Spanish and French sides, now fit for the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for great, and 'between' sets one plus that reversal inside the two articles; 'match' here means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eligible is suitable to marry, a good match; it also means qualified to play.

clue.text: No real alterations seen in 2, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 19, 22 across and 22 down

parts.note: nominal means in name only, not real
changes are alterations

explanation.surface: The clue claims that the listed entries contain only token alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: The listed entries each show a change of name: a person's pen name or a place renamed, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Every listed entry involves a name being swapped for another, which is exactly what changes of name are.

clue.text: Bill that is, over time, providing a crucial check

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: over means the outer piece covers the inner letter

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is

explanation.surface: An invoice, it turns out, after a while serves as a decisive test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts T inside IDEST.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test is a decisive trial, from the use of acid to prove gold.

clue.text: See 15
Maid of Orleans uplifted, guided and elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: bonne is French for maid, Orleans being a French city
led means guided

explanation.surface: Joan of Arc, the Maid of Orleans, raised up and guided, is exalted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maid of Orleans' wants to be Joan of Arc; it is just a French maid, BONNE, which 'uplifted' turns to ENNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ennobled is to be raised to the nobility, so elevated in rank.

clue.text: See 4
It's bad, tucking into something to eat — very bad

indicators.note: tucking into means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a dish is something to eat
evil is something bad

explanation.surface: Something wicked is gobbling up a meal, and it is truly nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, but it signals one piece going inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish means fiendishly wicked, so extremely bad.

clue.text: They are mostly awfully coarse

indicators.note: awfully means terribly, so the letters are thrown into disorder
mostly means all but the last letter is used

explanation.surface: Some people are described as, for the most part, terribly crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of THEYARE, and 'awfully' rearranges THEYAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude or vulgar, so earthy is a synonym for coarse.

clue.text: Name Dianne differently

indicators.note: differently means in another arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Dianne gets called by another name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges DIANNE into another girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadine is a woman's forename, so it is a name.

clue.text: Name taken by poet, strangely unread

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A poet's adopted name remains oddly unread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges UNREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Neruda was the pen name adopted by the Chilean poet Ricardo Eliécer Neftalí Reyes Basoalto.

clue.text: Scary thing, Frenchman turning on fellow conservative

parts.note: the right is the conservative side of politics

indicators.note: turning means read in reverse

parts.note: René is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman turns on a fellow Tory, which is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the French name, and 'on' places it after the fellow and the conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightener is something meant to scare, a threat or menace.

clue.text: Money deposited in bank safe, but only to begin with

indicators.note: only to begin with means just the opening letter of each word is used

explanation.surface: Cash is put into a bank's safe, but just at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only to begin with' takes the first letters of deposited, in, bank, safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Dibs is old British slang for money.

clue.text: See 12
Article by informal relative becoming academic text

parts.note: the is the definite article
sis is an informal word for sister

explanation.surface: A piece written by a sister turns into a scholarly work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' wants to be a written piece; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a long piece of academic writing submitted for a degree.

clue.text: Wrongly removed tube buried in one part of garden

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: a bed is a part of a garden for plants
a duct is a tube

explanation.surface: A pipe was taken away improperly and buried in a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried in' signals the tube going inside; 'Wrongly removed' suggests a mistaken extraction, but means kidnapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off illegally, so abducted means wrongly taken away.
